title: Kryvorivnia
summary: Kryvorivnia is a village located in the Verkhovyna Raion of the Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], recognized as a cultural center for the Hutsul people. It serves as a significant site for both summer and winter traditions among this ethnic group.

sections.heading: Geographical and Administrative Context
paragraphs: Kryvorivnia ([[ukrainian|Ukrainian]]: Криворівня) is situated within the Verkhovyna Raion, part of the [[ivano-frankivsk-oblast|Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast]] of [[ukraine|Ukraine]]. The village is integrated into the Verkhovyna settlement hromada, which is one of the administrative hromadas in the country.

sections.heading: Cultural Significance
paragraphs: Kryvorivnia is regarded as both the traditional summer and winter capital of the Hutsul people, highlighting its importance in the cultural practices and seasonal activities of this ethnic group.

sections.heading: Religious Heritage
paragraphs: The village is home to the Church of the Nativity of the Theotokos, a wooden structure built in 1719, which is part of the Orthodox Church of Ukraine (PCU). This church serves as a significant religious site for the local community.

sections.heading: Cinematic Connection
paragraphs: The village gained international recognition through the film 'Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors,' directed by Sergei Parajanov. The location where the film was shot has been transformed into a museum, preserving its cinematic legacy.

sections.heading: Notable Residents
paragraphs: Kryvorivnia has been the birthplace of notable figures such as Ivan Rybaruk (born 1966), a Ukrainian priest, writer, editor, and presenter, and Oleksa Volianskyi (1862–1947), a Ukrainian priest, ethnographer, and cultural activist, who contributed significantly to the cultural and educational landscape of Ukraine.
